- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially after recent price spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5% for high-peak periods.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >95), model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect; apply a “cool-down” adjustment: reduce forecast by 3–8% in the next 3–5 days post-spike.
- Sentiment history is uniformly neutral (0.00) across all examples — no sentiment-driven bias observed; ignore sentiment as a correction factor.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: forecasts often remain high for 3–5 days after a peak, then drop sharply — adjust by applying a 1–3 day lagged moving average to smooth out overconfidence.
- Forecast error is most severe in the 10–15 day window after the peak; apply a “decay factor” to reduce forecast weight by 10–20% for days 10–15 post-peak.
- No horizon-specific error detected; 30-day forecasts are consistently overconfident, especially in the first 7 days — reduce initial 7-day forecast by 5–10% to align with observed mean reversion.
